question: Which observable evidence supports which Android software-lineage or assurance claim, under what transformation and trust assumptions, when applications include third-party components and AI-mediated changes?
review_type: bounded claim-centered structured evidence synthesis with a closest-review adversary matrix
inclusion: Android artifact observations; component/version evidence; provenance, signing, transparency, repository, build, or reproducibility mechanisms mappable to an APK lifecycle; empirical supply-chain evidence; AI-mediated mobile generation or software-security evidence; and review/method sources structuring these areas.
exclusion: General LLM or GUI-agent work without a software-artifact lineage object; withdrawn or retracted publications from the active synthesis; stronger inferences not supported by the source observation; and cross-study performance pooling across incompatible oracles and denominators.
synthesis_rule: A mechanism is not promoted beyond the proposition directly observed under its reported assumptions; counter-histories and unknowns are retained.
gap_result: 75 located direct/partial cells, 41 scoped absences and 31 unresolved cells across 21 records. Seven Brereton cells await representation-aware admission; 24 other cells remain source-unresolved. Direct all-dimension coverage remains undetermined.
publication_status_boundary: Each active record has a checked scholarly or official locator and a corpus/BibTeX status match. This record-level check is not a comprehensive retraction-registry search. One known withdrawn work is quarantined in excluded_publications.csv and retained only in a historical regression fixture.
limitations: No independent second human coder or agreement statistic
Publisher-abstract coding is explicitly distinguished from full/selected-source coding
No primary model, malware, device, or human experiment
Record-level publication checks are not a comprehensive retraction-registry census
reproduction_scope: Offline scripts validate corpus/bibliography/extraction equality, canonical identifier and publication-status constraints, source-version/page and historical-to-current recoding bindings, matrix semantics, claim-ledger references, mutation controls, the retained finite bookkeeping oracle, and manuscript-facing counts. They do not validate source interpretation or novelty.
traceability_note: Every retained record has a direct scholarly or official locator, source-reading boundary, retrospective retained-record provenance row, and publication-status row. This does not reconstruct a complete database-search denominator. The legacy fresh_source_rechecks fields count cumulative dated ledger rows, not a new all-source recheck batch. Legacy reading-depth labels are not content certificates; selected fulltext checks and legacy-not-reverified records are counted separately.

supplementary_field_coding.boundary: Located coding is AI-assisted and same-process. Software checks bindings and calculations, not semantic understanding.

semantic_reading.boundary: Explicit same-process reading assessments bind the seven coded fields and exact retrieved source. Software verifies identities and counts, not understanding or final-publication equivalence.
